extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (K-12 school districts, colleges, universities), Title IX coordinators, institutional administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory preamble and final-regulation guidance for recipients on implementing §106.45 grievance procedures for Title IX sexual harassment, including notice, confidentiality, dismissal, supportive measures, and appeal/notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must allow parties to meaningfully participate in the grievance process by providing written notice of allegations to both parties where there is a formal complaint, including the details specified in this provision (including sufficient details known at the time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written notice must provide key information about the alleged incident so both parties understand the scope of the investigation and can prepare to meaningfully participate. The Department expects the written notice to include sufficient details known at the time (such as identity of parties, location, date, and nature of the misconduct) and now also must notify the parties of each party's right to an advisor of choice. The notice is required only after a formal complaint has been filed (or signed by a Title IX Coordinator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of written notice applies to Title IX sexual harassment as defined in §106.30
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice requirement applies to allegations that constitute sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 and to a grievance process that complies with §106.45 — not to all violations of a recipient's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule revises §106.45(b)(2) to remove references to a recipient's 'code of conduct' and explicitly tie the notice requirement to sexual harassment 'as defined in §106.30' and to the grievance process 'that complies with §106.45' to avoid confusion about applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of parents/legal guardians for elementary and secondary students
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include parents and legal guardians of elementary and secondary school students on lists of persons to whom recipients send notice and information about the recipient's non-discrimination policy and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(a) revised to include parents/guardians; §106.6(g) added to state nothing in the final regulations alters the legal right of parents or guardians to exercise rights on behalf of a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of medical, psychological, and similar records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are prohibited from accessing or using a party's medical, psychological, and similar records for a grievance process without the party's voluntary, written consent (or parent's consent if the party is not an 'eligible student').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added to §106.45(b)(5)(i): recipients must not use treatment records without written consent. This is intended to protect sensitive health information and comply with applicable State and Federal health care privacy laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation and limits on dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations add §106.71 prohibiting intimidation, threats, coercion, or discrimination against any individual for the purpose of interfering with any right secured by Title IX; recipients may warn parties not to discuss or disseminate allegations where such dissemination would constitute retaliation or unlawful tortious conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While parties have a right to discuss allegations under investigation, the recipient may caution against discussions that constitute retaliation. Recipients must respond to complaints of retaliation to protect complainants whose identities were disclosed as a result of a formal complaint or for implementation of supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party identities in written notice after a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: When a formal complaint has triggered a grievance process, the written notice of allegations must identify the parties (to the extent their identities are known); anonymity during the grievance process is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department requires party identities (to the extent known) to be included in the written notice of allegations so that both parties can meaningfully participate. The notice need not include other personally identifiable information (e.g., dates of birth, SSNs, home addresses). Prior to a formal complaint, recipients are not required to disclose a complainant's identity to a respondent except when necessary to provide a particular supportive measure (e.g., a mutual no-contact order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on disclosure while balancing safety/supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Although identities are required after a formal complaint, recipients must consider safety concerns and the complainant's wishes regarding supportive measures; emergency removal or certain supportive measures may justify disclosure of identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure of identity poses a risk of retaliation or danger to the complainant, Title IX Coordinators must discuss available supportive measures and consider complainant preferences. Emergency removal (§106.44(c)) or protective orders remain available. Recipients may implement supportive measures that require identifying the complainant when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to provide respondent the full formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to give respondents a copy of the complainant's written formal complaint; the written notice required by §106.45(b)(2) (date, time, alleged conduct, identity of complainant) is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters requested requiring the full complaint be shared; the Department declined, asserting the information required by §106.45(b)(2) provides sufficient opportunity for respondent participation while protecting privacy to the extent unrelated allegations may exist in the formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent silence and adverse inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Title IX requires depriving a person of rights protected by the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments; decision-makers must not draw inferences about responsibility from a party's failure or refusal to appear at a hearing or answer cross-examination questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added to §106.6(d)(2) and §106.45(b)(6)(i): respondents may remain silent when answers might implicate the right against self-incrimination; decision-makers must not treat silence or non-participation as evidence of guilt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of notice — 'sufficient time to prepare a response'
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation does not define a fixed time period but requires notice to be provided early enough to allow the respondent 'sufficient time to prepare a response'; this is a fact-specific determination constrained by the recipient's obligation to conduct the grievance process within designated, reasonably prompt time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will not interpret 'upon receipt' to mean 'immediately' and recognizes intake and compilation of details may take time. However, delaying notice could cause failure to meet timely process requirements. Failure to provide sufficient time may result in Department enforcement actions (remedial steps and possible risk to Federal funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory dismissal for lack of Title IX jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must dismiss a formal complaint (or allegations therein) for purposes of sexual harassment under Title IX when the allegations, if true, would not meet the jurisdictional conditions (i.e., not sexual harassment under §106.30, not against a person in the United States, or not in the recipient's education program or activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final §106.45(b)(3)(i) was revised to add 'against a person in the United States' and to clarify mandatory dismissal is only for Title IX purposes and 'does not preclude action under another provision of the recipient's code of conduct.' The recipient must send written notice of any dismissal decision and reason, and both parties have equal rights to appeal the dismissal (§106.45(b)(3)(iii) and revised §106.45(b)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted (discretionary) dismissal grounds and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are permitted (but not required) to dismiss a formal complaint in three specific circumstances: (1) the complainant provides written notice withdrawing the formal complaint or allegations; (2) the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed by the recipient; or (3) specific circumstances prevent the recipient from gathering evidence sufficient to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discretionary dismissal (§106.45(b)(3)(ii)) is narrow and does not authorize dismissal for 'frivolous' or 'meritless' allegations. It is intended to allow dismissal where completion of an investigation is futile (e.g., complainant refuses to participate but has not formally withdrawn; respondent outside authority of recipient). Discretionary dismissals must be distinguishable from premature determinations about burden of proof, which must be made only by the decision-maker following §§106.45(b)(5)-(7). Recipients must notify parties in writing of discretionary dismissals and reasons; parties may appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may question respondents without disclosing complainant identity but cannot discipline without grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may choose to question an employee-respondent about allegations without disclosing the complainant's identity, provided the recipient does not take disciplinary action without first applying the §106.45 grievance process (unless emergency removal or permitted administrative leave applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves some institutional investigatory flexibility, but disciplinary action triggering sanctions requires adherence to the grievance procedures unless exceptions (emergency removal §106.44(c), administrative leave §106.44(d)) apply.
